title: DTLSv1.3: support decryption
description:
First PR, comments and feedbacks are welcome!
caveats:
- max 10 epoch (10 KeyUpdate per side)
- No support for request_connection_id or new_connection_id type messages
- ~~CID not fully supported~~ CID is supported

Tested with:

[dtls13.pcapng](/uploads/699e75a4ed642ef9cdf660ffc1129c15/dtls13.pcapng)

[sslkeylog.log](/uploads/2bc8a3425130e340f71321f488e46229/sslkeylog.log)

Screenshot:
![image](/uploads/c94f459c45edc8ecef93c0c085034c50/image.png)

(will almost complete support for dtlsv1.3, see https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/18071)

M

In the end, I decided to move the check earlier to be uniform to the display of TLSv1.3 (with `Hello Retry Request` displayed in the info column without the `Server Hello` type).

Here's the two test files with the relevant secrets from the keylogfiles added to the pcapng as Decryption Secrets Blocks for easier testing. (Edit->Inject TLS Secrets).

[dtls13-dsb.pcapng](/uploads/c866c1a2a9688b1e160c9dd5fe9f57a6/dtls13-dsb.pcapng)

[dtls13-cid-psk-dsb.pcapng](/uploads/ac1a00851f5a762a6b37e56712af9ef1/dtls13-cid-psk-dsb.pcapng)

And here's the early data example:
[dtls13-earlydata-dsb.pcapng](/uploads/f7c1a69bc3e2b31e810df57b0b45da4a/dtls13-earlydata-dsb.pcapng)

From what I can tell, if the S bit is not set, then `hdr_length` is smaller (only include 1 byte for the size of the sequence length), but you're still using two bytes for it in `dec->dtls13_aad.data` (leaving the high byte uninitialized) so there's a buffer overflow.
fixing
Fixed in 58acd93c93be19e0960fb1de7182dbbf69b2c97f inside !15649
